stem: Why is a clean-to-dirty work sequence useful in cultivation biosecurity?
choices: It reduces the chance of carrying pests or pathogens from higher-risk areas into cleaner areas
It concentrates sanitation work near the end of the route, reducing interruptions while technicians visit cleaner crop areas
It keeps worker movement predictable, so scouting records remain comparable even when the same tools continue through the route
It shortens travel between rooms, and reduced travel distance is the main mechanism by which cross-contamination risk is lowered
rationale: Working from cleaner or lower-risk material toward dirtier or known-problem areas helps reduce movement of biological hazards into cleaner crop zones, especially when combined with appropriate sanitation and tool controls.
